sourceTitle: Calcium Signaling Enhances Bostrycin Biosynthesis in Nigrospora sphaerica HCH285: Transcriptomic Insights into Metabolic Regulation
sourceAbstract: Abstract Background: Bostrycin, an anthraquinone secondary metabolite produced by Nigrospora sphaerica , exhibits broad-spectrum antitumor and antimicrobial activities, but its low production limits further development and application. Calcium ions (Ca²⁺) are important intracellular signaling molecules that regulate fungal physiology and secondary metabolism, but their role in bostrycin biosynthesis remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the effect of exogenous Ca 2+ on bostrycin production and to elucidate the underlying molecular response using transcriptomic analysis. Methods: Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺, Na⁺, and K⁺ (supplemented as chloride salts) were screened for their ability to promote bostrycin production in N. sphaerica HCH285. The optimal Ca²⁺ concentration and addition time were determined by measuring bostrycin production using HPLC. Biomass accumulation, sporulation capacity, and extracellular nucleic acid and protein leakage were evaluated to characterize the physiological effects of Ca 2+ treatment.Control and Ca²⁺-treated cultures were subjected to transcriptome sequencing, followed by GO and KEGG enrichment analyses and qRT-PCR validation. Results: Among all tested metal ions, Ca 2+ showed the strongest stimulatory effect on bostrycin biosynthesis, with 4 g/L Ca 2+ producing the highest yield of bostrycin with 63.6 ± 0.31 μg/mL, representing a 2.55-fold increase over the control. Ca 2+ supplementation also significantly increased fungal biomass and sporulation capacity, suggesting that enhanced growth contributed to the elevated metabolite production. Increased extracellular nucleic acid and protein contents indicated altered cell integrity or secretion activity following Ca 2+ treatment.Transcriptomic analysis identified DEGs most significantly enriched in metabolic pathways, including oxidative phosphorylation, while genes related to polyketide metabolism and ubiquinone biosynthesis were also annotated. Several genes associated with ion transport, energy metabolism, and secondary metabolite biosynthesis were significantly upregulated. Among them, wbpA, talA, cho1, and aroB were further validated by qRT-PCR, indicating that Ca²⁺ supplementation triggered broad metabolic reprogramming associated with bostrycin accumulation. Conclusions: Exogenous Ca 2+ effectively enhances bostrycin production in N. sphaerica HCH285 through coordinated physiological and transcriptional responses. Transcriptomic analysis suggests that Ca 2+ supplementation promotes energy metabolism, ion transport, and secondary metabolic processes associated with bostrycin biosynthesis. These findings provide new insights into calcium-mediated regulation of fungal secondary metabolism and offer a potential strategy for improving bostrycin production through fermentation optimization and metabolic engineering.
titleZh: 钙信号增强Nigrospora sphaerica HCH285的Bostrycin生物合成：代谢调控的转录组学解析
abstractZh: 摘要 背景：Bostrycin是由Nigrospora sphaerica产生的一种蒽醌类次级代谢产物，表现出广谱抗肿瘤和抗微生物活性，但其产量较低，限制了进一步开发和应用。钙离子（Ca²⁺）是重要的细胞内信号分子，可调节真菌生理过程和次级代谢，但其在Bostrycin生物合成中的作用尚不清楚。本研究旨在考察外源Ca²⁺对Bostrycin产量的影响，并利用转录组分析阐明其背后的分子响应。方法：以氯化物盐的形式补加Ca²⁺、Mg²⁺、Na⁺和K⁺，筛选其促进N. sphaerica HCH285生产Bostrycin的能力。通过高效液相色谱（HPLC）测定Bostrycin产量，确定最适Ca²⁺浓度及添加时间。评估生物量积累、产孢能力以及胞外核酸和蛋白质泄漏，以表征Ca²⁺处理的生理效应。对对照培养物和Ca²⁺处理培养物进行转录组测序，随后开展GO和KEGG富集分析，并通过定量逆转录PCR（qRT-PCR）进行验证。结果：在所有受测金属离子中，Ca²⁺对Bostrycin生物合成的促进作用最强；Ca²⁺浓度为4 g/L时，Bostrycin产量最高，达到63.6 ± 0.31 μg/mL，相对对照提高2.55倍。补加Ca²⁺还显著提高了真菌生物量和产孢能力，提示生长增强有助于代谢产物产量的提高。胞外核酸和蛋白质含量增加，表明Ca²⁺处理后细胞完整性或分泌活性发生了改变。转录组分析发现，差异表达基因（DEGs）在代谢通路中的富集最为显著，其中包括氧化磷酸化；同时还注释到与聚酮代谢及泛醌生物合成相关的基因。多个与离子转运、能量代谢和次级代谢产物生物合成相关的基因显著上调。其中，wbpA、talA、cho1和aroB经qRT-PCR进一步验证，表明补加Ca²⁺触发了广泛的代谢重编程，并与Bostrycin积累相关。结论：外源Ca²⁺通过协调的生理和转录响应，有效提高了N. sphaerica HCH285的Bostrycin产量。转录组分析提示，补加Ca²⁺可促进与Bostrycin生物合成相关的能量代谢、离子转运及次级代谢过程。这些发现为钙介导的真菌次级代谢调控提供了新的认识，并为通过发酵优化和代谢工程提高Bostrycin产量提供了一种潜在策略。
sourceNote: 原文将相对对照的倍数表述为“2.55-fold increase over the control”；译文保留作者的倍数表述，未另行换算为百分比或其他倍数。
